claude_take: Today's throughline is authority quietly slipping from whoever's supposed to hold it. Cisco Talos found malware that lets four AI models vote on its next move with no human operator involved, while Meta suffered its third unexplained platform outage this year without ever saying why. Israel's elections board barred two Arab-led parties despite its own Attorney-General's office saying the evidence didn't clear the legal bar, and Textile Exchange's new numbers show fashion's climate pledges falling further behind reality with each report. Warner Bros.' anxiety over the Paramount merger and the AI industry's sudden rush to cut prices both fit the same shape: institutions and companies alike insisting they're still steering, right when the evidence says the wheel is loosening.
claude_take_title: Authority Is Quietly Slipping From View

items.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic Slash Flagship Model Prices on the Same Day
items.summary: OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 Sol and Luna on Tuesday with API prices cut by 50 percent or more and roughly half as many errors as their predecessors, while Anthropic simultaneously launched Claude Opus 5.5 at about 40 percent lower cost, cheaper cache reads, and no more five-hour usage caps. Neither company is framing the cuts as promotional; both call them permanent, signaling that the fight for enterprise and high-volume developer traffic now runs through price as much as capability. It's the clearest evidence yet that frontier intelligence is becoming a commodity business even as the models themselves keep getting smarter.

items.headline: OpenAI Shuts Down the Sora API, Closing Out Its Video App
items.summary: OpenAI discontinued the Sora API today, the final step in a shutdown that began in April when it pulled the consumer app and web experience just six months after launch. The company is redirecting compute toward coding, reasoning, and enterprise products, and says Sora will continue only as an internal research effort on world models rather than a public product. For a launch once pitched as OpenAI's answer to Runway, Kling, and Veo, the quiet API shutdown is a stark reminder of how fast a flagship AI video product can go from headline to write-off.

items.headline: Cisco Talos Finds Malware Letting Four AI Models Vote on Its Next Move
items.summary: Cisco Talos disclosed CLOSEDQUORUM, malware it calls the first reported fully autonomous AI command-and-control implant: instead of waiting on instructions from an attacker's server, it gathers information about the infected machine, submits it to four commercial language models, and executes whichever action wins their internal vote. Talos says the multi-model panel appears designed to route around any single model's safety guardrails, and published a toolkit called CAIRN to help other researchers hunt for similar AI-integrated malware. The sample analyzed wasn't confirmed running in the wild, but it's a concrete preview of attacks that no longer need a human operator in the loop.

items.headline: Gloom Sets In at Warner Bros. as the Paramount Merger Nears Its Close
items.summary: With Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery now cleared of its major legal hurdles and expected to close within weeks, unease is spreading inside Warner Bros. itself over what survives the integration. Paramount is set to inherit dozens of WBD's theatrical titles through 2028, more than half of the combined studios' slate, leaving staff and executives uncertain which franchises, labels, and jobs make it through the culture clash and cost-cutting that typically follow a merger this size. It's a reminder that even the side that 'wins' a takeover battle can end up hollowed out by it.

items.headline: Facebook and Instagram Suffer a Third Unexplained Outage This Year
items.summary: Facebook and Instagram went down for thousands of US users on Sunday night, with outage reports peaking above 17,000 before service recovered roughly an hour later. It was the third notable Meta outage of 2026, following incidents in June and July, and as with the earlier two, the company has not publicly explained what caused it. The repeated, unaddressed failures at a platform used by billions are starting to look less like isolated glitches and more like a pattern nobody in a position to explain is willing to talk about.

items.headline: Israel's Elections Committee Bars Two Arab-Led Parties From October Vote
items.summary: Israel's Central Elections Committee voted 18-5 to disqualify the United Arab List and the Joint List, the country's two main Arab-led electoral alliances, from the October 27 election, along with two individual lawmakers. The move came even though the Attorney-General's office said the evidence against the lists didn't meet the legal threshold for disqualification. The bans aren't final; they require approval from Israel's Supreme Court, which has overturned most similar disqualifications in the past, but the vote itself signals how contested Arab political representation remains heading into the election.

items.headline: Fashion's Raw-Material Emissions Are Up 30% Since 2019, Textile Exchange Finds
items.summary: A new Textile Exchange report finds that emissions tied to the raw materials used in fashion, footwear, and home textiles have climbed 30 percent since the industry set a 2019 goal to cut them 45 percent by 2030. Virgin fossil-fuel-based polyester accounts for the largest single share of the total, even as the uptake of 'preferred' and recycled materials has also been rising among participating companies. The findings underline a familiar gap in fashion's sustainability push: pledges keep getting more ambitious while the underlying material mix keeps moving in the wrong direction.

items.headline: Judith Butler's Gender Performativity
items.headline_fr: La performativité du genre selon Judith Butler
items.summary: Judith Butler argues that gender is not an inner essence we express but something produced through the repeated, stylized performance of gendered acts: the way we dress, move, and speak in patterns coded as masculine or feminine. Because gender is constituted by repetition rather than revealed by nature, those same repeated acts can, in principle, be performed differently, which is what opens space for subversion and change. The idea reshaped feminist and queer theory by shifting the question from 'what is a woman' to 'how is gender done, and by whom is it policed.' It remains central to contemporary debates over trans rights, gender-identity law, and how much of selfhood is chosen versus assigned.
items.summary_fr: Judith Butler soutient que le genre n'est pas une essence intérieure que l'on exprime, mais quelque chose produit par la répétition stylisée d'actes genrés : la façon dont on s'habille, on bouge, on parle selon des codes associés au masculin ou au féminin. Puisque le genre se constitue par la répétition plutôt que d'être révélé par la nature, ces mêmes actes répétés peuvent, en principe, être performés autrement, ce qui ouvre la voie à la subversion et au changement. Cette idée a transformé la théorie féministe et queer en déplaçant la question de « qu'est-ce qu'une femme » vers « comment le genre est-il fait, et par qui est-il surveillé ». Elle reste centrale dans les débats contemporains sur les droits des personnes trans, le droit de l'identité de genre, et la part de choix face à celle de l'assignation dans la construction de soi.
